contract_negotiation.description: The limitation of liability cap must not exceed 1x fees paid.
Indemnification must be limited to third-party claims arising from performance. No broad uncapped indemnities.
Firm retains ownership of pre-existing IP. Work product transfers on full payment.
contract_negotiation.acceptable_range: joint ownership with carve-out for pre-existing IP

contract_negotiation.description: Governing law must match the firm's primary jurisdiction or a neutral venue.
contract_negotiation.acceptable_range: any US state with well-developed commercial law

contract_negotiation.description: Confidentiality obligations must survive for a reasonable period after termination.
Non-compete must be reasonable in scope and duration. No blanket industry bans.
Contract must include termination for convenience with 30 days notice.
Data processing terms must reference applicable privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.).
Professional liability insurance must be maintained at specified minimums.
Payment within 30 days of invoice with interest on late payments.
Disputes must go through mediation before arbitration or litigation.
Assignment must require mutual consent; no unilateral assignment.

GDPR.requirement: Personal data must not be kept longer than necessary for the purpose for which it was collected.
Data subjects have the right to request deletion of personal data under specific conditions.
Data subjects can request their data in a structured, commonly used format.
Processing of personal data requires explicit, informed consent — silence or pre-ticked boxes are not valid.
Data breaches must be reported to supervisory authority within 72 hours of discovery.
A Data Protection Officer must be appointed if processing involves large-scale sensitive data or public authority.
Personal data transfers outside the EEA require adequate safeguards (SCCs, BCRs, adequacy decision).
Data Protection Impact Assessment required for high-risk processing activities.

CCPA.requirement: Consumers have the right to know what personal information is collected, used, shared, or sold.
Consumers can request deletion of personal information collected from them.
Consumers can opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information.
Businesses cannot discriminate against consumers who exercise their CCPA rights.
Collection, use, and retention of personal information must be reasonably necessary and proportionate.
Consumers can limit use of sensitive personal information (SSN, precise geolocation, biometric data).

SOC2.requirement: Logical and physical access controls must restrict system access to authorized users only.
All access to production systems and customer data must be logged and retained.
Production changes must be authorized, tested, and approved before deployment.
Customer data must be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256).
Documented incident response plan with defined roles, communication channels, and recovery procedures.
Third-party vendors with access to customer data must undergo security assessment and monitoring.

ISO27001.requirement: Information security risks must be identified, analyzed, and evaluated at planned intervals.
All information assets must be identified, classified, and assigned ownership.
An access control policy must be established, documented, and reviewed based on business and security requirements.
Information security requirements for suppliers must be agreed and documented.
Information security continuity must be embedded in the organization's business continuity management.
Event logs must be produced, kept, and regularly reviewed to record user activities and security events.
